question: How does an object come to be apprehended in nonconceptual self-awareness?
premises: There is a unity with the nonconceptual sense of I grasp.
In nonconceptual self-awareness the object flashes forth.
That flashing forth is the basis of apprehension.
inference: An object is apprehended in nonconceptual self-awareness through the sheer flashing forth of the object united with the sense of I grasp.
uncertainties: The compound gṛhṇāmītyavikalpaikyabalāt can be parsed in slightly different ways.
plain_english: By the force of unity with the nonconceptual sense of I grasp, the object is apprehended. In nonconceptual self-awareness, it is simply the flashing forth of the object that is known.
